worked_solution:
Using the properties of addition/subtraction and scalar multiplication of vectors to isolate the $l$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{a}_{1}+l{a}_{2} & =b \\ 5[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+l[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -15 \\ 25 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\ l[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -15 \\ 25 \\ 16\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ l[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 15 \\ -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

From the final equation above, we can tell that 
$l=3.$
